name: IRB Infrastructure Developers Ltd
title: IRB Infrastructure Developers Ltd - 532947 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: IRB Q2 FY27 PAT rose 85% YoY to ₹260 crore, with finance cost down 14% to ₹388 crore on deleveraging.
summary.overview: Consolidated income rose 8% YoY to ₹1,945 crore and EBITDA grew 13% to ₹1,102 crore in Q2 FY27. Lower finance cost and a sharp rise in InvIT distributions drove profit growth, while depreciation rose 26%. Management said the InvIT asset monetisation of ₹4,605 crore EV brought in ₹2,744 crore of non-dilutive equity consideration to the group. Bid activity on TOT projects restarted after a backstop MLFF compensation mechanism was firmed up by NHAI, but no BOT or HAM bid had been submitted yet.

financial_highlights.metric: Income from InvIT & related assets segment

segments.name: InvIT & related assets
segments.commentary: Segment income ₹356 crore, up 17% YoY. Private InvIT average daily toll collection was ₹13.1 crore vs ₹9.2 crore, about 42% growth on a like-for-like basis excluding 3 assets moved to Public InvIT.

segments.name: BOT (toll)
segments.commentary: Segment income ₹721 crore, up 15% YoY. Mumbai-Pune and Ahmedabad-Vadodara gross toll collections grew 14% and 16%, about 15% across the wholly owned portfolio.

segments.name: Construction (EPC)
segments.commentary: Segment income ₹821 crore, flat YoY. EPC order book stands at about ₹1,200 crore.

segments.name: Distributions to IRB
segments.commentary: Private InvIT declared ~₹231 crore; IRB's 51% share ~₹118 crore vs ₹26 crore (about 354% growth). Public InvIT declared ~₹269 crore; IRB's ~16% effective share ~₹43 crore vs ₹32 crore (about 35% growth).

guidance_outlook: Interest cost: management said the Q2 finance cost (₹388 crore) is the new quarterly run-rate and will decline further with scheduled SPV repayments.
Net debt-free status by FY30 is reaffirmed; management said interest cost will keep falling quarter after quarter.
O&M margin guidance of about 20% is maintained.
Cash ROE target of 8% to 14% over the next 4 to 5 years (ROE timeline cited as FY32 in the question) is reaffirmed, driven by operating leverage as debt amortises.
Asset base targeted at ₹1,40,000 crore by 2030 from ~₹94,000 crore currently.
Next set of TOT bids expected to be out soon and concluded before March 2027, per management's discussions with the authority.
capex_capacity: Asset base is about ₹94,000 crore with average concession life of about 20 years, per management.

Public InvIT (IRB InvIT Fund) acquired two operational highway assets from Private InvIT (IRB Infrastructure Trust) at aggregate EV of ₹4,605 crore; raised ₹2,000 crore equity, and IRB invested ₹351 crore in the preferential issue.
Capital recycling is said to position the group to pursue new opportunities worth about ₹8,000 crore.
Private InvIT originally had 9 projects; 5 have now moved to Public InvIT, leaving 4.
Two HAM projects on IRB's balance sheet are nearing completion, expected in about 6 months; they would then be eligible for transfer to Public InvIT.
Ganga Expressway completed during the year, now contributing to Private InvIT distributions.
demand_pricing: Management attributed toll growth to steady traffic demand and inflation-linked tariff mechanisms.
TOT bidding resumed after NHAI firmed up a backstop compensation mechanism for the multi-lane free flow (MLFF) system; three TOT bids that had been under bidding for a long time have been concluded.
Management said there is no BOT or HAM bid where IRB has submitted a bid so far, though it continues to evaluate opportunities.
On HAM/EPC, management was not sure recent concession agreement changes would keep out frivolous bidders.
Management said the low-hanging fruit in BOT is behind, and more complex BOT projects will be selected more carefully.
Total order book is about ₹43,400 crore, including EPC order book of about ₹1,200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of TOT and project awarding, and has bidding intensity changed with tighter criteria?
qa_highlights.answer: TOT bids were delayed over MLFF compensation talks, now resolved with a backstop mechanism from NHAI. Three long-pending TOT bids have been concluded and the next set is expected before March 2027. No BOT or HAM bid has been submitted yet.

qa_highlights.question: Is the lower interest cost the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, Q2 interest cost is the new run-rate. It fell due to the VM7 transfer to Public InvIT last year, SPV repayments at MP and AV, and a lower rate at IRB MP after refinancing; further declines are expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is there BOT toll opportunity ahead, or will the business rely on TOT and the backlog?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the low-hanging BOT fruit is over and it will be selective on complex projects. It sees asset monetisation as the focus and points to about 20 years of revenue visibility from the ₹94,000 crore asset base.

qa_highlights.question: Will IRB move into non-road businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stay in road and highway infrastructure and has no plans to diversify into unrelated businesses, citing a focus on picky project additions.

qa_highlights.question: Which Private InvIT or balance-sheet projects could transfer to Public InvIT soon?
qa_highlights.answer: Four projects remain in Private InvIT. Two HAM projects on IRB's balance sheet are nearing completion in about 6 months and would be eligible for transfer once criteria are met.

qa_highlights.question: Are the 20% O&M margin, net debt-free by FY30, and cash ROE of 8% to 14% targets still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed all three. It said operating leverage will lift cash ROEs from 8% to 14% over 4 to 5 years as debt falls and revenue grows at about 10% to 12% CAGR on completed projects.

risks_watch: Depreciation rose 26% YoY to ₹329 crore, which partly offset the gain from lower finance cost.
HAM and EPC bidding may attract weaker players despite revised concession terms; management is uncertain how effective the changes will be.
No new BOT or HAM bid submitted as of the call; growth beyond InvIT transfers and TOT depends on new awards.
Construction revenue was flat YoY at ₹821 crore, with a small EPC order book of about ₹1,200 crore.
Delivery on TOT bids before March 2027 and on the ₹8,000 crore opportunity pipeline.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on deleveraging, distributions and reaffirmed targets, but cautious on new BOT and HAM awards, where management declined to give details on bids. Answers on bid pipeline were brief, and the call was short with few questions.
key_quotes: So yes, you are right, this quarter's figure should be considered the new run-rate, and interest costs will reduce further in line with scheduled repayments.
So, since listing in 2008 we have always stayed away from all these glamorous ideas and always pursued the most non-glamorous or do more of the same kind of a concept all along.

adds.what: Two HAM projects on IRB's balance sheet nearing completion, eligible for transfer to Public InvIT
Ganga Expressway completed, now contributing to Private InvIT distributions

growth.why: Management reaffirmed the ₹1,40,000 crore asset base by 2030 (from ~₹94,000 crore), cash ROE of 8% to 14% in 4 to 5 years and O&M margin of ~20%, backed partly by ~₹43,400 crore total order book (EPC ~₹1,200 crore), two HAM projects due in ~6 months and toll growth of ~15%, but no BOT or HAM bid has been submitted yet and revenue grew only 8% in Q2 with construction flat.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Finance cost fell 14% YoY to ₹388 crore and management calls this the new run-rate, with further declines from SPV repayments; O&M margin guided at about 20% and held, while depreciation rose 26% to ₹329 crore partly offsetting gains.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Two HAM projects on IRB's balance sheet are nearing completion in about 6 months, and the Ganga Expressway is already completed, feeding Private InvIT distributions (IRB's 51% share ~₹118 crore vs ₹26 crore).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Toll collections grew about 15% across the wholly owned portfolio and Private InvIT daily toll rose to ₹13.1 crore from ₹9.2 crore (about 42% like-for-like), though total consolidated income grew only 8% and construction was flat at ₹821 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Asset base ~₹94,000 crore targeted at ₹1,40,000 crore by 2030 and about ₹8,000 crore of new opportunities cited, but no BOT or HAM bid has been submitted yet, so no firm new capex is visible.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held all targets (20% O&M margin, net debt-free by FY30, 8% to 14% cash ROE) without raising them, and revenue grew only 8% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Growth beyond InvIT transfers and TOT depends on new awards, no BOT or HAM bid is submitted, and management is uncertain whether revised HAM/EPC terms will keep out weaker bidders.

rows.label: TOT bids to be concluded before March 2027
rows.why: Three long-pending TOT bids were concluded and management expects the next set out soon and concluded before March 2027, though the order book is about ₹43,400 crore including only ~₹1,200 crore EPC.

rows.label: Private InvIT projects transfer to Public InvIT
rows.why: Private InvIT is down to 4 of 9 projects after 5 moved to Public InvIT, and the two HAM projects nearing completion in ~6 months would become eligible for transfer.

rows.label: Lower interest cost as debt amortises
rows.why: Q2 finance cost of ₹388 crore (down 14% YoY) is the new run-rate and management expects further declines from scheduled SPV repayments, supporting net debt-free by FY30.

tone.note: Management was confident on deleveraging, InvIT distributions and reaffirmed targets, but cautious on new BOT and HAM awards and declined to give bid details; the call was short with few analyst questions.
